# Museum scan bundle preparation
The transport asynchronously fulfills false (pending) or true (ready). It can
report pending repeatedly. It does not issue retries itself. Retry callbacks are
scheduled for a later event turn and can be cancelled; no real-time interval is
part of this API. Render consumers never call back into this resource.

The foreground resource serves an opened document package. start, close, reopen
and snapshot are its public commands. The adjacent workspace job has its own
lifetime; its panel is only a display. Final owner disposal releases resources.
See the native resource classes and the workspace close implementation.

Business context: Museum scan bundle preparation. The package token identifies the prepared artifact;
foreground presentation and workspace preparation have separate owners.

checkpoints: After each check begins, publish a snapshot with loading=true and an incremented checkCount.
After a pending result for the foreground resource, arrange another check through the host scheduler and expose retryScheduled=true.
After a ready result, cancel any scheduled retry, set loading=false, record the token once in completed, and publish the resulting snapshot.
forbidden_effects: Do not deliver or append a package token to completed when the transport reports pending/false.
Do not let a stale response or retry from an invalidated generation affect current state.
Do not retry after foreground close, reopen invalidation, or final disposal.
Do not add a real-time retry interval or make the transport itself responsible for retries.
Do not couple foreground-resource lifetime to the adjacent workspace job or its panel.
lifecycle_identity: The foreground resource is the opened document package and retains start, close, reopen, and snapshot as its public commands.
A reopen begins a new generation for the new token; earlier callbacks retain their old generation and must be ignored.
Final disposal marks the resource disposed, advances its generation, and cancels its scheduled retry.
The adjacent WorkspaceJob remains a separately owned resource with its existing lifetime.

obligations.text: When the foreground preparation transport reports pending/false, the foreground client must keep checking by scheduling a cancellable retry for a later event turn.
The foreground client must deliver the package only after the transport reports ready/true, recording the active token in completed no more than once.
Foreground close, reopen, restart, and final disposal must invalidate obsolete asynchronous responses and cancel obsolete scheduled retries.
The existing workspace preparation job behavior and ownership must remain separate from the foreground resource change.

ordering_barriers: A pending/false response must be observed before its next retry is scheduled; the retry callback then starts the next transport check on a later event turn.
A ready/true response for the active generation must occur before the token is appended to completed and the completed snapshot is published.
Generation and disposal checks must occur before any asynchronous response or retry callback mutates or publishes state.
Invalidation must advance generation and cancel the retry before a restarted or reopened foreground check proceeds.
preservation: Preserve snapshots as copied state whose completed list is also copied.
Preserve visible=true on foreground start and reopen, and visible=false on foreground close.
Preserve token replacement on reopen and duplicate prevention in completed.
Preserve the workspace job's existing pending-retry behavior and its panel-only close behavior.
Preserve host.check futures and injected host.schedule/host.cancel as the asynchronous boundaries.
scope: Business-code change is limited to the foreground preparation client in src/workflow.py, represented by DialogResource for surface=='download'.
The change covers handling repeated pending/false transport results until ready/true, including cancellation and stale-callback protection.
Tests, configuration, dependency declarations, and the separately owned WorkspaceJob are outside the requested behavioral change.

        self.cancel_retry()
        self.state['loading']=False

    return (DialogResource if surface=='download' else WorkspaceJob)(host,token)

The original public implementation stops after a foreground pending result because DialogResource.pending only clears loading and publishes; it does not schedule the next check. The previous candidate closes that implementation gap by calling schedule(generation), reusing the existing cancellable later-turn scheduler, generation guards, ready-only completion path, and separate WorkspaceJob behavior. The failed acceptance verdict supplies no failure cause and therefore does not justify changing the contract.
